newsitem.title: FINLAND: New method cuts Finnish jobless rate 0.5 pct pts.
newsitem.headline: New method cuts Finnish jobless rate 0.5 pct pts.

text.p: Finland's new method of calculating monthly unemployment figures will reduce the jobless rate in comparison with the old method by about half a percentage point, Statistics Finland (SF) said on Monday.
"The unemployment rate fell by about a half a percentage point (in comparison with the earlier figures)," statistician Salme Kiiski told a news conference.

The reform of the jobless statistics harmonises Finland's data with those published by the European Union statistical authority, Eurostat, and with concepts and definitions used by the EU and the International Labour Organisation (ILO).

The new method cuts the total number of unemployed -- and also the jobless rate -- by using tighter criteria for unemployed status and by counting workers laid off for fixed periods of time as part of the labour force, Kiiski said.

In January, according to the new method, unemployment was down to 16.7 percent from 17.4 in January 1996, with the year-ago statistic revised to make it comparable with the new figure, SF said in a statement.
By the old method, the January 1996 unemployment rate would be 17.8 percent, SF said. The December 1996 jobless rate would now be 15.5 percent instead of 15.1 percent by the new method.
While reducing the average number of unemployed by about 9,000 per month, the new method also boosts the total workforce by a good two percent, or about 49,000 people on average per month, SF said.
In January 1997 the total number of unemployed was 411,000, down from 431,000 in January 1996, SF said.
Calculated by the old method, the January 1996 figure would have been 438,000, statistician Timo Koskimaki said.
Statistics Finland is now revising the figures back at least to the beginning of the 1990s to make them comparable with the new data.
"We will soon have new revised figures for the whole of the 1990s," Koskimaki said, adding that the revision work would take about a month.
Even so, fully comparable figures will not be available until this time next year, as the revisions are estimates.
"For several months the comparison data will be less reliable than before," Koskimaki said.

Calculating by an entirely different method, the Finnish labour ministry earlier this month said January 1997 unemployment fell to 18.5 percent from 19.4 percent a year earlier And from 19.0 percent in December.
Statistics Finland data is used in international comparisons.
